## Question 1 (5 points)

Explain what a merge conflict is in Git and why it can occur when multiple people collaborate on the same repository. To answer this question, describe how the local repository and remote GitHub repository become out of sync, and explain how pull, resolving conflicts, stage, commit, and push fit into the process of managing changes collaboratively.

**A merge conflict occurs when multiple people make changes to the same part of a file in a shared Git repository, and Git cannot automatically combine those changes. Each collaborator works on their own local copy of the repository, while GitHub stores the shared remote version. When one person pushes their changes to GitHub, the other collaborators' local repositories become out of sync with the remote repository because they do not yet contain those updates. Before pushing their own changes, a collaborator must pull the latest version from GitHub. Git attempts to combine the changes, but if it encounters conflicting edits, the collaborator must manually resolve the conflict by deciding which changes to keep or how to combine them.**

## Question 2 (5 points)

Please see the following merge conflict:

```
# Calculate summary statistics

data <- c(12, 15, 18, 20, 25)

<<<<<<< HEAD
mean_value <- mean(data)
mean_value
=======
median_value <- median(data)
median_value
>>>>>>> origin/main
```


## Question 3 (10 points)

Before answering this question, create a code chunk only for your packages. Library the `tidyverse` package, and turn off the messages/warnings using the proper code chunk arguments. Next, answer the question below.

For this question, we are going to use the `Toothgrowth` data set in base R. If you would like more information about the `Toothgrowth` data set, please open up the help file. 

I want you to make a side-by-side boxplots with `Dose` on the y-axis, and `length` on the x-axis. Next, comment on the relationship between `Dose` and `length`. 

Note: Make sure that your boxplots are appropriately labeled with a title, x-axis, y-axis, and a caption that says *ToothGrowth from the datasets package*. 

Note: I want you to answer the coding part of this question **in a single pipeline**. 


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(tidyverse)

ToothGrowth |> 
  mutate(dose = factor(dose)) |>
  ggplot(
    aes(x = len, y = dose)
  ) + 
  geom_boxplot() + 
  labs(title = "Length vs Dosage in 60 guinea pigs",
       x = "Length of Tooth",
       y = "Dose",
       caption = "ToothGrowth from the datasets package")
```
